chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Woe to you, O Ibn Arafa! Work for the sake of other than showing off and other than being heard of. Indeed, whoever works for other than Allah, Allah will dismiss him to what he worked for. Woe to you! No one performs a deed except that Allah returns it to him; if it is good, it is good, and if it is evil, it is evil.'

key_terms.إِنْ خَيْراً فَخَيْرٌ: If good, then good (the return matches the deed)
key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Showing off (performing deeds to be seen by others)
key_terms.سُمْعَةٌ: Being heard of (performing deeds to be known/famous)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of performing deeds for show rather than for Allah?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) warns against riya' (showing off) and sum'ah (desire for fame), explaining that Allah 'entrusts' the doer to their own deed, meaning the deed itself becomes their recompense or burden. This concept, rooted in the famous hadith qudsi, highlights that insincere acts are returned to the doer as a consequence, whether good or evil, emphasizing the transformative power of intention in Shia spiritual theology.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Muhammad Bin Arafa who said,

‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Woe be unto you, O Ibn Arafa! For it is such that the one who does a deed for other than Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Allocate it to what he worked for. Woe be unto you! There is no deed which anyone does except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Returns it as such – so if it is good, so good, and if evil, so evil’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Muhammad ibn ‘Arafah who has said the following:

“Once al-Rida (a.s.) said to me, ‘Woe upon you, O ibn ‘Arafah, you must work without showing off and publicity; those who work for anyone other than Allah, He assigns him to whomever he has worked. Woe upon you, whatever one does, Allah returns it back, good (result) if it is good and evil (results) if it is bad.’”
